newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up despite China policy.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up despite China policy.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Friday despite news that Taiwan's top economic policymaker said it was time for local businessmen to slow their investments in mainland China, brokers said.
"It is time to slow our investment in the mainland," Chiang Ping-kun, chairman of the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development told Reuters.
The index ended up 45.95 points or 0.72 percent at an intraday high of 6,471.63. Turnover was a modest T$39.65 billion.
China-concept shares fell on Chiang's remarks, with President Enterprises down 30 cents T$41.5. Brokers noted late buying on transport and construction stocks.

"Chairman Chiang's remarks have been well expected, and the late buying showed that investors were more concerned about the rising foreign fund inflows since August," said George Hou of Jardine Fleming Securities.

Chiang's remarks came one day after the announcement by President Enterprises that it had abandoned plans to build a US$100 million power plant in China, and it would instead invest more than T$30 billion in local projects over two years.
"While Taiwan firms' China investments may slow, their strengthening local investments should boost the local economy," Hou said.
Domestic demand-oriented shares, such as constructions and steels rose.
Electronics rebounded after recent falls, with Acer up 70 cents to T$39.4.
Brokers said they expected a firming trend in coming sessions as sentiment remains bullish on foreign fund inflows.
For Saturday, the index is seen testing resistance at 6,500.
